Concepts

Five or six directions for each view, using sample data. These are unpicked prototypes for review.

Overview

Tasks board
Tasks board 1
Studio columns
The classic stage board taken to its finest finish, where every card, column and drag feels as sure-footed as Linear and as friendly as Trello.
Tasks board 2
Who's carrying what
A board sliced by person, so a small team sees at a glance who is overloaded, who is free, and hands work across with a single drag.
Tasks board 3
Today's desk
A focus board that clears everything away except today: a queue of what is up next, a small hand of at most three things you are working, and a real pile of what you finished.
Tasks board 4
Flow and friction
A board that shows time as well as place, so stuck, ageing work and bottlenecked stages surface themselves before anyone has to ask.
Tasks board 5
The planning wall
A spatial board that feels like the wall of sticky notes a team stands in front of, where you can think freely and one press tidies it into trackable columns and back.
Tasks list
Tasks list 1
Keyboard command list
A dense, single-line list you drive entirely from the keyboard, where a command line at the foot of the page turns plain sentences into edits across everything you have selected.
Tasks list 2
Living outline
Tasks are a nested outline you can zoom into, where every parent rolls up the progress of everything beneath it, so the list shows the shape of the plan and not just its items.
Tasks list 3
Planner's sheet
A true spreadsheet for planners who think in columns, with cell-level selection, fill-down, typed columns like budget and headcount, and live totals, so the task list doubles as the event's working sheet.
Tasks list 4
Today, next, later
The list is organised by when you will do something, not by its status, with an honest capacity meter for today and a short daily ritual that turns a pile of tasks into a plan you can finish.
Tasks list 5
Who owes what
Every task is a plain sentence of who promised what, for whom and by when, grouped by person, and every part of it is a word you can click to change.
Tasks calendar
Tasks calendar 1
The living month
A month grid made to Fantastical's standard, where how busy each day is and what runs over several days read at a glance, and a plain sentence typed at the top lands on the right day as you write it.
Tasks calendar 2
Plan my week
A time-blocking planner where you pull tasks from a tray into real hours, and each day shows honestly whether the plan fits the time you have.
Tasks calendar 3
Team load
A calendar turned on its side, with people as rows and days as columns, so a small team can see who is overloaded on which day and rebalance by dragging work from one person to another.
Tasks calendar 4
Countdown runway
For work that builds to one big date, the calendar becomes a countdown runway where every week is labelled by how far it is from the day, and you can always see whether you are on track to get there.
Tasks calendar 5
The agenda river
One calm stream of days that merges tasks, milestones and events in reading order, folds quiet stretches into a single line and keeps today anchored, so the calendar reads like a well-edited diary rather than a grid.
Analytics
Analytics 1
The Friday letter
Analytics as a short, warm letter from a good project manager, written fresh each Friday, with word-sized charts set into the sentences and a margin that lights up the exact bar a phrase refers to.
Analytics 2
Will we make it
One question answered with one picture: a landing forecast of when the remaining work finishes against the big date, and plain-English levers that visibly slide it.
Analytics 3
Who needs a hand
Each person's coming weeks stack up as tiles against their own usual pace, so anyone can see whose pile spills over and drag work to someone with room.
Analytics 4
Project replay
Replay the whole Project day by day on a simple board, with the moments that changed its course pinned to the timeline, so you can watch how it got here instead of reading about it.
Analytics 5
Ask a question
A question-first page where you pick or type what you want to know and get back one plain sentence and the one chart that proves it, chained into a thread of follow-ups you can pin.
Analytics 6
All projects wall
A calm wall of identical small multiples puts every Project side by side on the same scales, with one crosshair that lights the same week on all of them, for the owner who wants to compare everything.
Apps and tools
Apps and tools 1
Your tool shelf
Apps and tools becomes a home screen you arrange like a phone, where every tool that is on shows as a small live widget, so being on and being useful look like the same thing.
Apps and tools 2
The shadow board
Each Project gets a workshop shadow board laid out for what it is, where tools that are on hang in place and tools that would help show only as a labelled outline, so what is missing is as visible as what is there.
Apps and tools 3
The field guide
Apps and tools reads like a beautifully kept field guide, where each tool is introduced through a short true story of how a team like yours used it, and every story can be tried on your own Project in place.
Apps and tools 4
Ask for a tool
Instead of browsing, you say what you need in your own words and the right tool assembles itself in front of you, previewed with your Project's own data, before you decide to keep it.
Apps and tools 5
The workbench
Tools are not a destination but a second pane: you open them beside your tasks and timeline, work across both at once, and save the arrangement as a bench you come back to.
Apps and tools 6
How it all connects
Apps and tools becomes a calm, living map of what talks to what, where your email, WhatsApp, calendars, forms and files visibly feed your Projects, so turning something on means drawing a line and watching real things start to flow.
Shared timeline
Shared timeline 1
The Road There
The shared timeline as a story read top to bottom, one chapter per milestone, with a sticky path that fills to today and a countdown that ends at the day.
Shared timeline 2
Countdown Instrument
One precise, ticking dial where a single turn is the whole project, so the shared page feels like the minutes before a launch and anyone can drag the hand back through what already happened.
Shared timeline 3
The Invitation Suite
The timeline arrives as a printed stationery suite: tap the wax seal and the envelope opens into one card for each moment on the way to the day.
Shared timeline 4
Every Day Poster
The shared timeline as a living poster: every day of the project is one dot, filled up to today, laid out to be screenshotted, saved and posted.
Shared timeline 5
The Dispatch
The shared timeline as a quiet run of letters from the people organising it, so stakeholders follow the progress the way they would follow a friend's news.
Shared timeline 6
The Line
The journey drawn as a transit map, where each strand of work is a coloured line running into the day, milestones are stations, and small trains show exactly where things are right now.
In development. You’re seeing it early.
×

Apps and tools 1
Your tool shelf
Apps and tools becomes a home screen you arrange like a phone, where every tool that is on shows as a small live widget, so being on and being useful look like the same thing.
Apps and tools 2
The shadow board
Each Project gets a workshop shadow board laid out for what it is, where tools that are on hang in place and tools that would help show only as a labelled outline, so what is missing is as visible as what is there.
Apps and tools 3
The field guide
Apps and tools reads like a beautifully kept field guide, where each tool is introduced through a short true story of how a team like yours used it, and every story can be tried on your own Project in place.
Apps and tools 4
Ask for a tool
Instead of browsing, you say what you need in your own words and the right tool assembles itself in front of you, previewed with your Project's own data, before you decide to keep it.
Apps and tools 5
The workbench
Tools are not a destination but a second pane: you open them beside your tasks and timeline, work across both at once, and save the arrangement as a bench you come back to.
Apps and tools 6
How it all connects
Apps and tools becomes a calm, living map of what talks to what, where your email, WhatsApp, calendars, forms and files visibly feed your Projects, so turning something on means drawing a line and watching real things start to flow.
Shared timeline
Shared timeline 1
The Road There
The shared timeline as a story read top to bottom, one chapter per milestone, with a sticky path that fills to today and a countdown that ends at the day.
Shared timeline 2
Countdown Instrument
One precise, ticking dial where a single turn is the whole project, so the shared page feels like the minutes before a launch and anyone can drag the hand back through what already happened.
Shared timeline 3
The Invitation Suite
The timeline arrives as a printed stationery suite: tap the wax seal and the envelope opens into one card for each moment on the way to the day.
Shared timeline 4
Every Day Poster
The shared timeline as a living poster: every day of the project is one dot, filled up to today, laid out to be screenshotted, saved and posted.
Shared timeline 5
The Dispatch
The shared timeline as a quiet run of letters from the people organising it, so stakeholders follow the progress the way they would follow a friend's news.
Shared timeline 6
The Line
The journey drawn as a transit map, where each strand of work is a coloured line running into the day, milestones are stations, and small trains show exactly where things are right now.
In development. You’re seeing it early.
